Native account IDs are rebound to caller=123456789012 and other=222222222222. Local bucket creation/public-block setup restores capture prerequisites; it is not evidence of extra native operations.

Reopen, malformed replacement after an admitted policy, private/public replacement on the sparse AP, empty-PAB public admission, and absence of inherited tags/policy after recreation are local transition regressions composed from the cited native contracts, not additional AWS captures.
Native MaxResults=0 and 1001 succeeded on small collections; these scenarios make no claim about clamping above 1000.
Native foreign-account AccessDenied cases target nonexistent names as the original owner actor; they do not establish a universal caller/account mismatch rule.
VPC policies with wildcard principals are classified nonpublic even with bucket/AP public-policy blocks enabled; exterior data access is separately denied. This is not positive VPC transport support.
RemainingNativeGaps: Raw empty VpcConfiguration is retained as InvalidRequest in control-isolated/raw-empty-vpc but omitted from SDK replay because the modeled VpcId requirement can reject before transport.
Exact 50, 51 and 52 character inputs are retained; the native labels name-50/name-51 are off by one. No three-character minimum claim is made.
Empty tag-key raw call was a signer failure and is not asserted.
Deleted ARN/alias summaries retain native codes and status but have no wire request ID; this lower-provenance capture is identified explicitly.
